subject: microbiology
title: Bacterial Surface Structures: Capsule, Flagella, Pili and Spores

steps.tx: The bacterial **capsule** is a hydrated polysaccharide (occasionally polypeptide, as in anthrax poly D glutamic acid) gel outside the wall that phagocytes cannot grip, making it the classic antiphagocytic virulence factor of pneumococcus, meningococcus, Hib and Klebsiella. Capsular antigens define serotypes, carry conjugate vaccines, and swell visibly with specific antiserum in the Quellung reaction Neufeld described in pneumococcus.
steps.say: A slippery sugar coat defeats phagocyte grip; vaccines learned to target the coat itself.

right.title: Capsule demonstrations
points: Quellung reaction: capsular swelling with antiserum

steps.tx: **Flagella** are helical flagellin propellers driven by a rotary motor, arranged peritrichously (all around, E coli and Salmonella), polar (Vibrio, Pseudomonas), lophotrichous tufts or amphitrichous, powering motility and chemotaxis. H antigens in Salmonella serotyping are flagellar, darting motility names Vibrio cholerae under the microscope, and swarming names Proteus across the agar plate.
steps.say: Name the flagellar pattern and the motility; H antigen is flagellin in serotyping language.

left.title: Arrangements
points: Non motile: Klebsiella, Shigella, Yersinia at 37C

right.title: Bedside clues
points: Swarming film over blood agar: Proteus
Hanging drop motility in cholera stool

steps.tx: **Pili** (fimbriae) are adhesive hair like protein appendages: common pili mediate attachment to mucosa (E coli P pili to uroepithelium, gonococcal pili with antigenic variation), while the single sex pilus of F plasmid donors builds the bridge of conjugation. Adhesion is colonisation's first step, so pili are vaccine and anti adhesion targets, and their phase variation lets pathogens shuffle surface identity.
steps.say: Pili grip the mucosa first and conjugate second; colonisation begins with adhesion.

left.title: Common pili
points: Type IV pili: twitching motility, Neisseria
Anti adhesion strategies in vaccine design

steps.tx: Bacterial **spores** (endospores) are dormant, dehydrated fortresses formed inside Bacillus and Clostridium cells under starvation: calcium dipicolinate core, keratin like coat, DNA armoured by small acid soluble proteins, surviving boiling, desiccation and years of soil. Germination returns the vegetative cell when nutrients reappear. Spores explain tetanus in wounds, anthrax persistence and why sterilisation standards are written against them.
steps.say: An endospore is a bacterium's time capsule; sterilisation is certified against its survival.

left.title: Spore anatomy
points: Core: DNA, calcium dipicolinate, low water
Terminal, subterminal or central positions identify

steps.tx: **Spore resistance writes** disinfection law: boiling and most disinfectants fail, so moist heat at 121 degrees under pressure, hot air at 160 to 180, ethylene oxide and sporicidal agents (glutaraldehyde prolonged, peracetic acid, hypochlorite) carry the spore claim, and biological indicators use Geobacillus stearothermophilus spores precisely because anything that kills them certifies the cycle. Alcohol hand rubs do not kill C difficile spores; soap and water physically removes them.
steps.say: If it cannot kill stearothermophilus spores, it has not sterilised; alcohol cannot, soap removes.

nodes.label: Biological indicator spores killed: cycle certified
Failure leaves spores to germinate in host or broth

steps.tx: The glycocalyx spectrum extends capsule logic into **biofilms**: slime layers anchoring communities to catheters, prostheses and teeth, where matrix polymers slow antibiotic penetration and metabolism slows killing, so device infections relapse until the device is removed. Staphylococcus epidermidis on lines and Pseudomonas in cystic fibrosis airways are biofilm diseases wearing organism names.
steps.say: A biofilm is a capsule become a city; antibiotics besiege it, removal conquers it.

left.title: Biofilm properties
points: Device removal usually required for cure

steps.tx: **Surface antigens organise** serotyping grammar: O antigen is the gram negative outer membrane polysaccharide side chain (somatic, heat stable), H is flagellar (heat labile), K is capsular (Vi in Salmonella Typhi masking O agglutination until heated), and F is fimbrial. Weil Felix and Widal reactions from the serology lessons are these letters at work in the test tube.
steps.say: O is wall sugar, H is flagellum, K is capsule; serology questions are alphabet questions.

left.title: Antigen letters
points: K and Vi: capsular, mask O antigen

right.title: Where letters work
points: E coli O157 and other pathotypes
Widal reads O and H titres

steps.tx: **Spore position and** capsule presence become rapid bench identities: terminal drumstick spores name tetani in a wound Gram stain, large boxcar bacilli with capsule in blood name anthracis, mucoid pink colonies on MacConkey whisper capsulated Klebsiella, and non motile capsulated coccobacilli in CSF answer Hib in the unvaccinated. Morphology lessons earn their marks at exactly these pattern recognitions.
steps.say: Drumstick, boxcar, mucoid: morphology patterns are diagnoses at bench speed.

left.title: Pattern identities
points: Boxcar bacilli with capsule: B anthracis
Sporing in culture, not tissue: clostridia usually

right.title: Bench cautions
points: Spores rarely seen in clinical specimens
Confirm patterns with culture and tests
